sources.title: Vishal Monga, Yuelong Li, and Yonina C. Eldar, Algorithm Unrolling: Interpretable, Efficient Deep Learning for Signal and Image Processing
sources.locator: Full 27-page paper, §II-C 'Algorithm Unrolling in General' and §IV-E subsection 'Convergence and Optimality Analysis of LISTA'.

contents.name: Section II-C: map each iteration to a layer, stack a finite number of layers, and train layer parameters end-to-end.
Section IV-E: LISTA convergence analyses impose additional structural and parameter conditions.

sources.title: Karol Gregor and Yann LeCun, Learning Fast Approximations of Sparse Coding
sources.locator: Full 8-page paper, §2.1, opening of §3, §3.3, and Algorithms 3–4.

contents.name: Section 3: a fixed-depth trainable encoder minimizes average squared code error on the training samples.

Section 3.3 and Algorithms 3–4: LISTA has a fixed number of forward layers and differentiates that finite encoder; the authors caution that extending trained LISTA beyond its trained depth has no convergence guarantee.

sources.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, full lecture notes
sources.locator: Full 137-page lecture notes, Chapter 7 §§7.1–7.2, printed pp. 65–67 / PDF pp. 69–71; Lemma 7.1 and the complete proof of Theorem 7.2.

contents.name: Lemma 7.1: the finite Landweber prefix has an explicit operator-polynomial formula.
Theorem 7.2 and the following exact-data discussion: Landweber convergence and early stopping are tied to separate range, noise, and step-size hypotheses.

sources.title: Terence Tao, An Introduction to Measure Theory, preliminary full-text book
sources.locator: Full 265-page preliminary book, Chapter 1 §1.4, Remark 1.4.33, printed p. 96 / PDF p. 111: composition of measurable morphisms is measurable.

contents.name: Remark 1.4.33: measurable morphisms are closed under composition.

sources.title: Vishal Monga, Yuelong Li, and Yonina C. Eldar, Algorithm Unrolling: Interpretable, Efficient Deep Learning for Signal and Image Processing
sources.locator: Full 27-page paper, §II-C 'Algorithm Unrolling in General' and §IV-E subsection 'Convergence and Optimality Analysis of LISTA'.

contents.name: Section II-C: finite iterative-layer cascades can use independently trained layer parameters.
Section IV-E: convergence results concern architectures with additional coupling and regularity hypotheses.

sources.title: Karol Gregor and Yann LeCun, Learning Fast Approximations of Sparse Coding
sources.locator: Full 8-page paper, §2.1, opening of §3, §3.3, and Algorithms 3–4.

contents.name: Sections 2.1 and 3.3: compare a conventional finite iterative recurrence with a fixed-depth learned encoder and its separate layer parameters.

sources.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, full lecture notes
sources.locator: Full 137-page lecture notes, Chapter 7 §§7.1–7.2, printed pp. 65–67 / PDF pp. 69–71; Lemma 7.1 and the complete proof of Theorem 7.2.

contents.name: Lemma 7.1 and Theorem 7.2: finite Landweber values are polynomial prefixes, with exact-data convergence under a separate step-size and range condition.

sources.title: Hongkai Zheng et al., InverseBench: Benchmarking Plug-and-Play Diffusion Priors for Inverse Problems in Physical Sciences
sources.locator: Full versioned 29-page ICLR 2025 paper, §4.3 question 'How well do PnPDP methods handle out-of-distribution sources?' and Figure 5, pp. 9–10.

contents.name: Figure 5 and the accompanying text: the tested methods show prior-feature bias on the paper's black-hole digit inputs and nine-cell inverse-scattering sources when trained on one-to-six-cell images.

sources.title: Giannis Daras et al., A Survey on Diffusion Models for Inverse Problems
sources.locator: Full versioned 38-page survey, §3.3 opening and Conclusion, printed pp. 18 and 25.

contents.name: Section 3.3 and Conclusion: selected posterior-sampling methods are called asymptotically exact only in method-specific infinite-computation limits, while practical scaling remains unresolved.
